page: Google Cloud Platform n2-highcpu-8 is an x86_64 architecture server belonging to the N2 family. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.8 GHz, configured with 4 physical cores and 2 threads per core. The system is equipped with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 1.0 GB per core ratio. It does not include local storage or integrated GPUs.

Benchmark data indicates average performance across several multi-core and utility operations. The server achieves average ratings in stress-ng multi-core CPU performance, PassMark CPU score, and software compilation with Clang. Memory bandwidth tests for both cached small blocks and uncached large blocks also fall into the average tier. However, single-core performance is weak, as demonstrated by lower-tier results in stress-ng single-core, gzip compression, and bzip3 decompression.

The primary architectural tradeoff of the n2-highcpu-8 is its low memory-to-CPU ratio. With only 1.0 GB of RAM per vCPU, memory-intensive workloads will experience bottlenecks, a limitation reflected in its weak PassMark memory score. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, this profile is optimized for compute-heavy tasks that do not require large memory footprints, allowing users to avoid paying for excess RAM.

This server is best suited for workloads such as static web serving, Redis database operations, and light software compilation, where multi-threaded CPU capacity is required but memory demands remain low. It is also capable of handling basic LLM inference for small models, though it is not suited for larger model architectures due to memory and hardware accelerator constraints.
